newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa's doctors hope for rapid recovery.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa's doctors hope for rapid recovery.

text.p: Mother Teresa said her morning prayers seated in a hospital chair on Tuesday, and doctors said they were optimistic the 86-year-old nun would quickly recover from heart surgery.
"She is fine," said Dr D.P. Shetty, head of the medical panel treating the Roman Catholic missionary at the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta.
"I am hopeful that she will recover very soon," he told Reuters.
Shetty said Mother Teresa sat up in a chair and said her prayers soon after she woke up. Then she took morning tea. "She had a good sleep and she is much better than on Sunday."
Mother Teresa, revered as a living saint for her work with the poor, the homeless and the terminally ill, had surgery to clear two blocked arteries last week.
It was the third time in five years that Mother Teresa, fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had undergone coronary surgery.
She had her first heart operation in the United States in 1991 and her second at the Birla centre in 1993.
She spent the weekend battling a long-standing lung problem and weak kidneys. She also had bronchial pneumonia.
On Sunday, clinic officials said doctors were concerned the problems would set back her recovery.
But they have since grown more optimistic she will soon return to her Missionaries of Charity religious order.
"She is stable," S.K. Tiwari, administrator of the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre, said on Tuesday.
Mother Teresa's doctors were to issue the next medical bulletin at around noon (0630 GMT), Tiwari said.
Born of Albanian parents as Agnes Gonxhe Bojaxhi, Mother Teresa was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of Missionaries of Charity, founded by Mother Teresa in 1949 and now with about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries, prayed for her recovery.
Dozens of nuns gathered for mass in "Mother House", as the order's headquarters is called, early on Tuesday. They prayed for more than an hour.
"Please pray for our Holy Father (Pope John Paul II) and our dearest mother's speedy recovery," read a chalked message on a blackboard outside the chapel.
